mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% over the prior month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, no significant negative 20-day forward returns occur when FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold upward; p-value of t-test > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) above the prior month's level by at least 2,000 suggests labor market strengthening, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where PAYEMS rises by <2,000, the forward return is not statistically higher than the prior window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST (residential construction) exceeds the prior month by 5% or more, it indicates accelerating demand for capital goods, which predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 10 consecutive 60-day windows with HOUST growth ≥5%, no significant positive 20-day forward returns observed (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% signals supply-side weakness, which is expected to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month INDPRO * 0.97 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In supply contraction regimes, no negative 5-day forward returns occur when INDPRO declines by ≥3% (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE fall simultaneously by at least 0.2% and 0.1% respectively in a month, the combined effect of lower rates and lower labor costs is expected to drive a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < previous month FEDFUNDS - 0.2% AND UNRATE < previous month UNRATE - 0.1%
regime_hint: Dual easing in rates and unemployment
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return when both triggers are met (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL inflation drop below 2% for three consecutive months is interpreted as a deflationary trend, which should be associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Deflation periods do not yield statistically significant positive 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP) grows by more than 4% in a quarter compared to the prior quarter, it reflects robust demand, which should be associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: No positive 20-day forward return occurs when quarterly GDP growth exceeds 4% (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp spike in RSAFS (retail sales) above the 90th percentile of the prior 12 months' values predicts excess demand for consumer goods, which should produce a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: No negative 20-day forward returns when RSAFS spikes above the 90th percentile (p-value > 0.05).
